candidates.title: One-Shot Training for Reduction of Performance Variance in LLM Rotation Quantization
candidates.venue: Digital Signal Processing and Signal Processing Education Workshop
candidates.abstract: Rotation-based quantization techniques have emerged as effective methods for compressing Large Language Models by mitigating the impact of activation outliers. However, existing approaches face significant challenges: random rotation methods like QuaRot exhibit substantial performance variability across different random seeds, while learned rotation methods like SpinQuant require hundreds of calibration samples, increasing the training cost. To address these limitations, we propose OneRot, a novel one-shot rotation-based quantization technique that achieves stable performance with only a single calibration sample. OneRot introduces random perturbations to layer activations during training, which amplify gradients and enable effective rotation matrix learning in a single attempt while simulating diverse activation distributions. Experimental results on Llama-2 7B, Llama-3.2 3B, and Llama-3.2 1B models with 4-bit quantization demonstrate that OneRot reduces perplexity by $0.25,2.88$, and 21.48, respectively, compared to QuaRot, and reduces standard deviation by $0.01,0.24$, and 1.41, respectively, while achieving comparable performance to SpinQuant using 800 times fewer samples. OneRot provides a practical solution for efficient LLM deployment by combining the stability of learned rotations with the computational efficiency of random approaches.
candidates.reason: OneRot。1校正サンプルの活性化へランダム摂動を加え、Cayley SGDで回転行列を学習。QuaRotの乱数依存とSpinQuantの多数サンプル校正の間を埋める。著者公開カメラレディ全文のWikiText-2評価でLlama-2 7B/Llama-3.2 3B/1Bの4bit W-A-KV量子化を検証し、QuaRot比perplexityをそれぞれ0.25/2.88/21.48改善、10 seedの標準偏差を0.01/0.24/1.41低減。SpinQuant比校正サンプル数800分の1。推論速度の改善率を報告したものではなく、主眼は量子化の品質と校正効率。

candidates.title: Semantics-Aware Scheduling for Low-Latency LLM Serving in Heterogeneous Computing Networks
candidates.venue: International Conference on Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing
candidates.abstract: The autoregressive nature of Large Language Models (LLMs) inference introduces inherent workload uncertainty, leading to severe head-of-line blocking and resource underutilization, particularly in heterogeneous computing networks. Existing LLM inference scheduling paradigms typically rely on large-scale neural predictors, incurring additional overhead and making it difficult to balance prediction cost against task scheduling efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel semantics-aware scheduling framework that predicts LLM inference workloads using LiPER, a lightweight prompt-enhanced response length predictor. We design LiPER as a small-scale language model by framing response-length estimation as a semantic classification problem. Specifically, LiPER encodes the prompt and directly predicts a discrete length bin with negligible inference overhead. Building on fine-grained workload priors, we propose LiPER-Sched, a discrete deep reinforcement-learning scheduler. By embedding predicted workloads into the system state, LiPER-Sched proactively dispatches tasks across heterogeneous computing nodes to improve load balance and minimize end-to-end latency. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets and simulated clusters show that our framework outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. LiPER-Sched cuts P99 tail latency by 45% over rule-based heuristics and converges to oracle-level performance with ground-truth information.
candidates.reason: LiPERがプロンプト意味表現から出力長を離散ビンとして低オーバーヘッド予測し、LiPER-Schedがその推定を状態に組み込んだ離散DRLで異種計算ノードへの要求配置を最適化する。IEEE会議版正式要旨ではルールベース手法比P99 tail latencyを45%削減。これは評価した実データと模擬クラスタにおける比較であり、全環境の保証ではない。

candidates.title: AG-BiLLM: Activation-Guided Fully Binarized Large Language Models
candidates.venue: International Conference on Electronics, Information and Communications
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are attracting attention in various fields with remarkable performance as their size becomes enormous. However, deploying LLMs in memory-limited environments is very difficult due to their vast number of parameters. Binarization, a method of representing parameters in 1-bit, can efficiently represent LLMs in terms of memory. Previous LLMs binarization studies used the Hessian matrix but faced several limitations. To overcome those limitations, we apply activation awareness to binarization by determining the saliency of weight columns using activation magnitude. Our method reduces perplexity by up to 87% compared to previous studies.
candidates.reason: 1bit LLM重み量子化で従来のHessianベース重要度に代えて活性化の大きさから重み列のsaliencyを判定する。IEEE出版社要旨では比較対象の従来手法よりperplexityを最大87%低減したと報告。特定評価設定での相対的品質改善であり、モデル全体の推論速度・メモリ削減率の直接実測値とは区別する。

candidates.title: VIFMM: Custom RISC-V Vector Instructions with INT-FP Mixed-Precision Computing for Accelerating LLM Inference
candidates.venue: IEEE International Conference on High Performance Computing and Communications
candidates.abstract: Weight-only quantization has been demonstrated to be an effective method to reduce memory and storage requirements for large language model (LLMs) deployed on resourceconstrained edge devices. However, it introduces frequent mixed precision operations between interger (INT) weights and floatingpoint (FP) activations. Conventional solutions typically quantize FP activations or dequantize INT weights during inference, which can degrade numerical accuracy and incur additional software overhead, ultimately slowing down inference. To eliminate this overhead, we propose VIFMM, an instruction set architecture (ISA) solution based on RISC-V vector (RVV) extension, supporting INT-FP mixed-precision computing, especially for operations between INT weights and FP activations, avoiding non-negligible data conversion in software. We implement VIFMM based on Ara, an open-source RVV core, along with a hardwarebased precision compensation mechanism to reuse the integer multiply accumulate calculation (MAC) units, to reduce hardware consumption and increase data precision. Experimental results show that VIFMM improves inference speed by 4%, with only 1.13% increase in hardware resource and 0.67% increase in power consumption, compared to conventional vector instructions. These findings illustrate that architecture-level support for INT-FP mixed-precision operations can significantly enhance LLM inference efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.
